title: 9 Young Scientists to Watch: the Timmerman Traverse Fellows at Damon Runyon - TimmermanReport.com
gist: Timmerman Traverse, a philanthropic hiking program run by biotech executives and investors, has raised $3.9 million since 2024 for Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation and is naming nine early-career fellows whose projects span CAR-T engineering, AML blood biomarkers, glioblastoma drug delivery, and CRISPR-based cancer research.

themes.theme: Philanthropic backstop for basic cancer research

insights.claim: Timmerman Traverse, a program of biotech executives and investors doing trips like Kilimanjaro and Everest Base Camp, has raised $3.9 million since 2024 for high-risk/high-reward cancer research via the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Tracks a growing philanthropic capital channel from biotech industry insiders into early, high-risk academic science that sits upstream of VC-backed spinouts.
insights.quote: Teams of biotech executives and investors have raised $3.9 million for high-risk/high-reward cancer research since 2024 as part of the Timmerman Traverse for Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation.

insights.claim: The author frames private/industry philanthropic funding of basic cancer research as an increasingly necessary backstop given the tenuous state of federal research funding.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Signals a structural funding gap risk in US biomedical basic research that private and philanthropic capital is stepping in to partially fill.
insights.quote: Our community’s steadfast support of science is more important than ever given the tenuous state of federal research funding.

insights.claim: Shaohua Zhang at UC San Francisco is engineering T cells with synthetic cell adhesion molecules (synCAMs) intended to make it harder for tumor cells to escape engineered CAR-T cells, with potential extension to macrophage, NK, and T-regulatory cell therapies.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: A synCAM platform that reduces tumor antigen escape could become a licensable module across multiple engineered cell therapy modalities beyond CAR-T.
insights.quote: The hope is that synCAMs will make it harder for tumor cells to escape from engineered CAR-T cells.

insights.claim: Stephanie Gaglione at the Gladstone Institutes is comprehensively profiling antigens displayed by virally-driven cancers to find new immune-response-provoking targets for T cell immunotherapies and cancer vaccines.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: A viral-cancer antigen atlas could feed target discovery pipelines for immuno-oncology and cancer vaccine developers.

insights.claim: Lachelle Weeks at Dana Farber Cancer Institute is searching blood samples for telltale signs that could let doctors predict when a patient is likely to develop acute myeloid leukemia (AML) before onset.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: A validated pre-AML blood biomarker would open a liquid-biopsy screening market for one of the toughest-to-treat blood cancers.

themes.theme: Novel chemistry and drug target discovery

insights.claim: Antonio LaPorte at Harvard is developing new synthesis techniques for sulfated sugars to study how these cell-surface molecules interact with and facilitate cancer cell growth and spread.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: New synthetic access to sulfated glycans could unlock a historically hard-to-drug target class relevant to tumor metastasis.

insights.claim: Angelos Pistofidis at MIT is investigating transcription termination factor 2 (TTF2) as a potential target for new cancer drugs.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Flags a specific, named early-stage oncology drug target (TTF2) worth tracking for future licensing or spinout activity out of MIT.

insights.claim: Shihui Chen at Caltech is using mouse embryo models to study how developmental pathways are hijacked during cancer initiation and progression, focusing on the regulator CARM1 which controls gene expression programs driving cell fate.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: CARM1-driven developmental hijacking work could surface a new epigenetic-regulator drug target class for oncology.

themes.theme: Blood-brain barrier drug delivery for glioblastoma

insights.claim: Natasha O'Brown at Rutgers is using zebrafish as a model organism to test methods for temporarily crossing the blood-brain barrier with small molecules, aimed at glioblastoma treatment.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: A validated transient BBB-crossing method would address one of oncology's hardest drug-delivery bottlenecks, a high-unmet-need area of major pharma interest.

insights.claim: Tata Kavlashvili at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center is studying how common mitochondrial DNA deletions contribute to both mitochondrial disorders and cancer, with research published in BioRxiv on July 17.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Links mitochondrial genomic instability to two distinct disease markets (rare mitochondrial disorders and cancer), a dual-indication target for genomics diagnostics.

insights.claim: Bailey Schultz at The Rockefeller University is using genome-wide CRISPR-based approaches to identify genes that regulate mycobacterial cell growth and division, studying the relationship between tuberculosis and cancer.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: CRISPR-based host-pathogen screening tools built for TB-cancer links could generalize to other infection-associated cancer research platforms.
